title: Spec of a purely inseparable extension is integral, universally injective and surjective
statement: Let $k\subset k'$ be a purely inseparable field extension [def-pc-field-tower] [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension], and let $\pi:\operatorname{Spec}k'\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ be the morphism of schemes induced by the inclusion $k\to k'$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Then $\pi$ is integral [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], universally injective [def-weil-radicial-morphism] and surjective [def-weil-surjective-morphism].

source.place: Morphisms, Lemma 01S4 (morphisms-lemma-universally-injective: radicial iff universally injective), applied to $\operatorname{Spec}k'\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, a one-point map with purely inseparable residue field extension; integrality: Algebra Section 0BR5 (algebra-section-universal-homeomorphism), opening paragraph (purely inseparable means algebraic)
